server.name: app-review-intel-mcp
server.instructions: App Store review intelligence. Use search_apps to find an app id, get_app_reviews for raw reviews, review_insights for rating distribution / version trends / complaint keywords, and compare_apps for side-by-side metrics. All data comes from Apple's public iTunes endpoints; review feeds expose at most the 500 most recent (or most helpful) reviews per country.

tools.name: search_apps
tools.title: Search App Store apps
tools.description: Search the Apple App Store for apps by keyword. Returns app ids, names, developers, ratings, rating counts, price, current version and store URL. Use the returned id with the review tools.

term.description: Search keywords, e.g. 'photo editor' or an app name

country.description: 2-letter App Store storefront code, e.g. "us", "gb", "de". Default "us".

tools.name: get_app_reviews
tools.title: Get App Store reviews
tools.description: Fetch customer reviews for an App Store app from Apple's public review feed. Returns normalized reviews (id, author, rating, title, body, version, date). Each page holds up to 50 reviews; Apple serves at most 10 pages.

app_id.description: App Store numeric id (e.g. 284882215), "id284882215", or an apps.apple.com URL

country.description: 2-letter App Store storefront code, e.g. "us", "gb", "de". Default "us".

pages.description: Number of review feed pages to fetch (1-10, ~50 reviews each). Default 1.

tools.name: review_insights
tools.title: Review insights
tools.description: Aggregate recent reviews of an app across one or more storefronts: rating distribution, average rating by app version (newest first), top complaint keywords/phrases from 1-2 star reviews (stopword-filtered 1-3 word n-grams ranked by how many reviews mention them), and representative negative/positive quotes.

app_id.description: App Store numeric id (e.g. 284882215), "id284882215", or an apps.apple.com URL

countries.description: Storefronts to aggregate, e.g. ["us","gb","ca"]. Default ["us"]. Max 10.

pages.description: Number of review feed pages to fetch (1-10, ~50 reviews each). Default 3.

keyword_limit.description: Number of complaint keywords to return

tools.name: compare_apps
tools.title: Compare apps
tools.description: Side-by-side comparison of 2-10 App Store apps in one storefront: store rating & rating count, price, size, current version & release date, plus metrics from recent reviews (sample average, % negative/positive, latest-version average, top complaint keywords). Includes per-metric leaders.

items.description: App Store numeric id (e.g. 284882215), "id284882215", or an apps.apple.com URL

country.description: 2-letter App Store storefront code, e.g. "us", "gb", "de". Default "us".

pages.description: Number of review feed pages to fetch (1-10, ~50 reviews each). Default 2.

reviews.author: JJLin283
reviews.title: Questionable security and no human being to talk to about it!
reviews.body:
I wouldn’t be writing this review, if I had been capable of talking to actual person! In the middle of the night, while I was asleep, someone succeeded at hacking into one of my Instagram accounts…after only two failed attempts! At the time of the first two attempts, which, again, happened while I was asleep, Instagram sent codes to my phone. On the third attempt, a message was sent to me via WhatsApp, informing me that my account had been accessed. That was just after 2AM. 

When I discovered these messages, after I woke up, at around 8AM, I clicked on a link that required me to verify whether it was me who had logged in. I, of course, clicked on “This wasn’t me.” Nothing happened! Every time I tried clicking on that option, a message popped up saying, “Something went wrong. Please try again.” It just said that over and over again. I was horrified. I had two Instagram accounts. The one that was hacked into, I simply deleted because I wasn’t using it that much anyway. 

The big problem is, the account that was hacked into was connected to my other, more important account, as well as my Facebook profile. I wonder what information the hacker stole! Lord knows, they had plenty of time to take whatever they wanted! The most I could do was chat with an AI bot about it! I gave this app two stars, instead of one, only because there is plenty about Instagram that I actually like, but what is it worth to have such a social media account when things like this can happen so easily?!

reviews.author: bw1226
reviews.title: Algorithm, stories, and login/security need some work
reviews.body:
I’ve been on insta for quite a while, but I’ve noticed that some of the features (noticeably the ones that are also shared, or should I say dominated by other apps) need improvement.
1) Close friends stories. Why can I only have one? If the goal was to implement similar features to sn*pchat, then why can’t I have multiple close friends for different friend groups/family/business partners? It’s been years since this feature has been available on other apps and Meta has made no effort to improve upon it, opting instead for location mapping (which most don’t use due to larger following or public accounts) and Instagram notes (attention seeking).
2) Login/security. Why can I not connect my iCloud account to Meta and use it to log in? From anecdotes, many of my friends have had their instagrams hacked, but it seems like iCloud is generally harder for scammers to access…additionally, getting locked out of my Instagram accounts has happened to me more than once. Meta should consider implementing this feature like other social media apps have.
3) finally, the algorithm isn’t as good as other social media apps. Understandably some, including myself, may be concerned about the lack of privacy and the information Meta is obtaining. However, given how much information is already available to them upon making an account, I would expect higher quality content on reels and suggested posts than what I am currently seeing.
More than willing to adjust my review should I see these features implemented.

reviews.title: Instagram plz fix this issue. Not only is it annoying but it’s also very very VERY frustrating!!!
reviews.body: I started using this app about several years ago and back then everything worked perfectly, but in these last couple of years, it has been hard to defend this app. There are some major major flaws, and it’s starting to get frustrating. Instagram used to be my #1 favorite app and I’d easily give it a 5 star rating and would recommend it to anyone who didn’t already have it, but now with all these tech issues, it’s hard to recommend it to people who are interested in getting it. For example, Instagram will randomly just crash sometimes and you won’t be able to receive or send any DMs, you can’t refresh your feed, if you try to log out and log back in, then you get the error message and there are a couple of other things as well. Instagram needs to figure this stuff out and fix it because it gets even more frustrating with each day that passes because you can’t see any DMs. This app used to be great and it ran so smoothly and flawlessly, but now it isn’t working as well as it used to. And, I also feel that Instagram is trying to add so many bells and whistles that it’s starting to turn into every other app that we use. I thought Instagram was supposed to be unique and fun in its own way, but I guess they want to be just another average app that everyone has on their phone. Instagram, please fix this issue that’s been happening for a long time now. It may not happen to everyone who has it, but for the people that it does happen to, you have to find a way to resolve it!!!
